general_background.title: Microwave coupling and heating
general_background.summary: Microwave fields couple to materials through their electrical response and can heat different parts of a reaction mixture differently. Polarization and mobile charges dissipate field energy, so heating depends on the liquid, dissolved species and other absorbing materials.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.

general_background.title: Solvent and transport
general_background.summary: A solvent carries dissolved species and transports heat through a reaction or dispersion. Solubility, viscosity and molecular interactions affect how precursors and ligand-coated particles move and mix.
